# k0rdent_service_accounts (Data Source)

Every service account in an organization, or at one scope in it.

Use it to see which accounts exist, what roles each holds, and whether it's still `active`. The provider reads service accounts and doesn't make them: the platform refuses to create an account or a credential for a `client_credentials` login, which is the only login the provider has.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Every service account in an organization, and the roles each holds.

data "k0rdent_service_accounts" "all" {
  organization_id = "org-ml-platform"
}

output "roles_by_account" {
  value = {
    for sa in data.k0rdent_service_accounts.all.service_accounts :
    "${sa.display_name} (${sa.scope} ${sa.scope_id})" => sa.roles
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `organization_id` (String) Organization to search. The service account operations are all inside one. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL. String length must be at most 63.

### Optional

- `display_name_regex` (String) Return only the accounts whose `display_name` matches this regular expression, in the RE2 syntax Terraform's own `regex` function takes. The match isn't anchored, so `prod` finds `preprod-a`: write `^prod-` for a prefix. One with no `display_name` never matches. Filtered in the provider, after the whole list is read: the list operation takes no such filter. **Constraints:** Must be a regular expression in RE2 syntax.
- `scope` (String) Search only the accounts at this level: `organization`, `folder` or `project`. Left out, the organization's own accounts and those of every project in it are searched. A folder's accounts are found only by naming the folder, since the contract has no operation that lists folders. **Constraints:** Value must be one of: ["organization" "folder" "project"].
- `scope_id` (String) What `scope` names: a folder id for `folder`, a project id for `project`. For `organization` it's the organization's id, and that's the default. **Known gap.** The contract declares no folder operation, so a folder's id can't be read. The [hardcoded values](../guides/hardcoded-values.md) guide names the side that has to change. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL. String length must be at most 63.
- `status` (String) Return only the accounts whose `status` is this value. Filtered in the provider, after the whole list is read: the list operation takes no such filter. **Constraints:** Value must be one of: ["active" "disabled"].

### Read-Only

- `service_accounts` (Attributes List) The accounts, in id order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--service_accounts))

<a id="nestedatt--service_accounts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `service_accounts`

Read-Only:

- `active_credential_count` (Number) Credentials that haven't expired, of the five an account can hold.
- `client_id` (String) The OAuth2 client id the account authenticates with.
- `created_at` (String) When it was created, as RFC 3339.
- `created_by` (String) The user id of the administrator who created it.
- `description` (String) What the account is for, if anyone said.
- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name the account is shown under.
- `id` (String) The service account's id, which `k0rdent_service_account` reads one by.
- `roles` (Set of String) Role slugs bound to the account at its scope.
- `scope` (String) The level its roles apply at: `organization`, `folder` or `project`.
- `scope_id` (String) The organization, folder or project `scope` names.
- `self_link` (String) Platform-defined reference to this service account.
- `status` (String) `active`, or `disabled`, in which case no credential of it mints a token.
- `updated_at` (String) When it last changed, as RFC 3339.
